newsitem.title: USA: Boeing plans two-for-one stock split.
newsitem.headline: Boeing plans two-for-one stock split.

text.p: Boeing Co. said Tuesday it planned a two-for-one stock split pending approval by shareholders.
The world's biggest commercial jet maker said its board had approved the plan and shareholders will vote on it at their annual meeting April 28.
"The board believes that a stock split will result in a market price for Boeing stock that will be attractive to a broader spectrum of investors," company Chairman Phil Condit said in a statement.
"It also will assure the availability of sufficient common stock for various corporate purposes such as financing and stock dividends," he said.
Boeing stock rose 75 cents to $106.25 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said they had expected a stock split for some time because the company historically has taken the action when its shares rose into the $90 or $100 range.
"It does send a strong signal to the market that management is optmistic about the company's prospects going forward," said Peter Jacobs, an analyst at Ragen MacKenzie.

Boeing last split its stock in 1990, just before a deep industry recession that forced the company to slash its work force by one-third. Since early 1995, Boeing stock has climbed steadily from the mid-$40 level.
The planned stock split would be effective June 13 for shareholders of record at the close of business May 16, a Boeing spokesman said.
Jacobs said he saw a good chance that Boeing would increase its common stock dividend after the completion of its proposed acquisition of McDonnell Douglas Corp., expected by the end of summer.
He pointed out that Boeing's cash hoard would grow to $7 billion to $8 billion by the end of the year from $5.3 billion at the end of 1996.

Under federal regulations governing stock-swap transactions such as the proposed McDonnell Douglas purchase, Boeing would be prohibited from offering any stock buybacks or special dividends for two years after completion of the merger.
